children.text:
Existing “agents” was hard to use and too closely tied to automations legacy UI.

Functionalities missing: Permissions were limited to lists not able to operate throughout the whole Workspace. No concept of connectors, multiple triggers, we now had chat.

Time to start from scratch and reimagine Agents and Teammates: the technology had progressed to the point we could really transform users workflows and interact with agents like coworkers in their workspace.

layers.text:
Builder is Unintuitive: The builder design remains unintuitive, especially for new users. Core steps are often missed or misconfigured, and the added complexity of Agents makes this worse. (Not new, we see this when we test Automations)

Entry Point Is Confusing: Confusion between Automate and Agents—those starting in Automations struggled more and rated the experience lower, highlighting a disconnect in navigation.

Agent Setup Lacks Clarity: Users struggled with setup, always overlooked Add Tools, and were unsure what was needed from them in each section. The dense layout led to skipped steps and setup errors. We asked them what was confusing and these were some of their responses—watch clip.

Overall, this tested pretty poorly—users consistently rated Ease of Use and Confidence pretty low, even after being walked through how to set things up.   I think the known challenges we have in the Automations builder greatly contribute to this, along with entry point confusion and an overwhelming amount of steps/info.

layers.text: The initial chat experience of setting up felt off. There were a lot of back and forths, and the follow ups were tedious. As we got initial versions of the agent experience working in staging, we were able to work with engineers to refine the chat UX, include follow up UI, and find other UX issues like when the agent would insert links into the response that led users away from the setup experience. This stage was user tested heavily, still it can be tedious to setup and requires continued refinement.

layers.text:
our prompt engineer proposed the ux here response: 
Phase 1 categorizes the user into low/medium/high opinion. 

Phase 2 is where the real iterative loop lives. The Builder calls a Draft Agent tool that writes a preliminary instruction set and simultaneously identifies placeholders for missing info. 

Phase 3 (Prompt Optimizer) runs as a sub-agent after creation to enrich the dry, logistical instructions with more human-like, integrative language for creative tasks.

Post-creation, users can refine through DMs or @mentions per the Refine your Super Agent help article, and the agent updates its own config.
